selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: S.J. Res. 7 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to officially disapprove and cancel a Federal Communications Commission rule titled 'Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program.' If enacted, the rule will have no force or effect.

affected_groups.effect: Will no longer be permitted under the specific FCC rule to use the E-Rate program to purchase discounted Wi-Fi hotspots and mobile connectivity for off-premises use by students, staff, and library patrons.
Will lose access to off-premises Wi-Fi hotspots and mobile connectivity services provided through the E-Rate program under the nullified rule.
affected_groups.group: Students, School Staff, and Library Patrons

key_provisions: Expresses congressional disapproval of the FCC rule titled 'Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program' published on August 20, 2024.
Declares that the disapproved FCC rule shall have no force or effect.
missing_information: The text does not specify any alternative programs or replacement rules for addressing the homework gap.
The text does not detail any financial costs or savings associated with nullifying the rule.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S.J. Res. 7 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to officially disapprove and cancel a Federal Communications Commission rule titled 'Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program.' If enacted, the rule will have no force or effect.
summary_detail.significance: This resolution voids an FCC policy that allowed E-Rate funds to pay for off-premises Wi-Fi hotspots, directly reversing the agency's attempt to address the homework gap.

title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Federal Communications Commission relating to "Addressing the Homework Gap Through the E-Rate Program".
